title: Ealing Emergency Help Points
summary: 24/7 emergency hospitals, urgent treatment centres, and local hazards across Ealing borough.
content:
For immediate life-threatening medical emergencies, always dial 999 first.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals with A&E
- Ealing Hospital: Uxbridge Road, Southall, UB1 3HW. From Hanwell station: ~15 min walk west along Uxbridge Road (A4020), or take bus 83, 207, 427, or SL8 (Superloop) heading west.
- Major Trauma Centre: St Mary's Hospital, Praed Street, Paddington, W2 1NY (serving North West London). From Ealing Broadway station: Elizabeth line or Great Western Railway direct to London Paddington (~12 mins).
- Northwick Park Hospital: Watford Road, Harrow, HA1 3UJ (serving northern Ealing/Greenford). From Greenford station: bus 92 directly to the hospital grounds.

2. Urgent Treatment Centres (Walk-In)
- Ealing Urgent Treatment Centre: Uxbridge Road, Southall, UB1 3HW (located inside Ealing Hospital main entrance). Open 24/7 for minor injuries and urgent conditions.

3. Local Area Hazard Notes
- River Brent: designated flood corridors run through Brent Valley Park, Hanwell, Perivale, and Greenford; avoid underpasses and river paths during prolonged downpours.
- Grand Union Canal: low-lying towpaths between Southall, Hanwell flight of locks, and Norwood Green can overflow during surge events.

4. Essential Supplies During Outages
Pharmacies and major grocery stores on The Broadway (Ealing), Uxbridge Road (West Ealing and Southall), Acton High Street, and Greenford Broadway supply bottled water, batteries, and essential medicines.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
